sections.content: You know the *ser* passive, passive *se* and *estar* + a participle from B2 Unit 20, and how to choose between them and the active verb. News reports use each for a different job. The *ser* passive names the doer when the doer matters: *Dos personas fueron rescatadas por los bomberos.* Passive *se* leaves the doer out: *Se cortaron las calles del centro.* With *a* and a person, the verb stays singular, as you saw in C1 Unit 2: *Se detuvo a dos personas.* *Estar* + a participle gives the state at the time of writing: *Las calles están cortadas.* Ask who matters, and whether you report the action or the state.

sections.title: Four ways, four jobs
rows: El sospechoso fue detenido por la policía.
The suspect was arrested by the police. (the doer is named)
Two people were arrested. (no doer; a + person, singular verb)
Se cortaron las calles del centro.
The streets of the centre were closed. (no doer; the verb agrees with the thing)
Las calles del centro están cortadas.
The streets of the centre are closed. (the state now)

items.spanish: Dos personas fueron rescatadas por los bomberos.
items.english: Two people were rescued by the firefighters.

items.spanish: Se detuvo a un sospechoso en la zona.
items.english: A suspect was arrested in the area.

items.spanish: Se cortó el tráfico en el puente.
items.english: Traffic was stopped on the bridge.

items.spanish: El puente sigue cortado al tráfico.
items.english: The bridge is still closed to traffic.

sections.content: English news uses "was arrested" and "were closed" for everything. In Spanish, choose: the doer named, *fue detenido por la policía*; the doer left out, *se detuvo a dos personas*; the state now, *está cortado*. Do not combine *se* with *por* and a doer: *Se detuvo a dos personas por la policía* is wrong.
